title: Her pianist Jerry and his stage seizures
summary: Her current pianist Jerry stopped drinking on doctor's orders. She describes a concert in Chicago where he stopped playing, and says he has something like seizures.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah, well now Jerry suits you beautifully but you've got a little problem there too sometimes.
Well I used to have a problem but Jerry doesn't drink anymore.
Oh, I didn't know. Oh, he doesn't.

And I know when we were in Chicago and I'm standing up there just singing and Jerry just stopped playing and I'm standing by the piano and I say, 'what's the matter? What's the matter?' And he says, 'what you singing'. And then he starts playing and he played in another key and I don't know what he's playing now. So now I got to try and find him.

But I mean he did that once. And then different people used to ask me, they'd say, 'what's the matter with Jerry?' And he sits at the piano and his eyes go rolling around in his head. He used to have some kind of, I forget what you call it now.

It was something that happens to your, you know, like a seizure.
A friend of his told me that. He said, 'well you know he has these seizures Helen'. I said, 'no I didn't know it'. I didn't know nothing about it.
You don't want a seizure when you're out on stage.

And it looked like he was about to have one. And people would ask me, what's wrong with him. I said, what do you mean, what's wrong with him? Nothing is wrong with him. His eyes would roll in his head and he ain't playing right. I said, I guess he just don't feel good.
But since he went on the wagen, that has improved, hasn't it?
Yeah. The doctor told him he better get on it.
Oh, well that's good. So Jerry, is he going to open with you at The Cookery?
Well I hope so. If he don't then I'm
